claims.text: Depositing a tungsten-based refractory HEA coating on Cu followed by annealing will form a graded intermetallic layer at the coating/substrate interface.
The graded intermetallic interface will enhance adhesion of the HEA coating to Cu.
The graded interface and HEA coating will enhance the wear resistance of the Cu substrate.
Cu has low inherent wear resistance.
A tungsten-based refractory HEA, such as a W-Ta system, can be deposited on Cu by laser cladding or sputter deposition.
Post-deposition annealing can promote interdiffusion at the Cu/HEA interface without degrading the HEA coating.
The interfacial layer may contain Cu-Ta intermetallic compounds.
Thermal treatment causes controlled interdiffusion and in situ formation of the intermetallic mediator layer.
The intermetallic mediator layer provides metallurgical bonding between the Cu substrate and the HEA coating.
A graded interfacial layer mitigates thermal-expansion mismatch between the Cu substrate and the HEA coating.
The HEA surface is hard and contributes to increased wear resistance.
Annealed HEA-coated Cu will have a lower wear rate than uncoated Cu and Cu carrying a coating without the mediating layer.
Annealed HEA-coated Cu will have higher coating adhesion strength than a comparable coating lacking the mediating layer.
The annealed HEA coating will show minimal delamination under mechanical stress.
Uncoated Cu exhibits poor wear resistance under comparable loading conditions.
The proposed benefit depends on annealing conditions that produce the interfacial intermetallic or graded layer.
Insufficient interdiffusion will fail to produce the proposed graded interface.
Overly aggressive thermal cycling can damage the HEA microstructure.
